name: MoC-001
description: Replace failing feed pump P-101 with upgraded unit
title: Feed Pump (P-101) Replacement
hazop_justification: HAZOP not required: Like-for-like pump replacement with no change to process design limits, control philosophy, or operating envelope; existing HAZOP remains valid. PSSR required: installing new equipment prior to start-up.
engineering_risks: Temporary instability in flow during start-up or switch-over. Lack of correspondence with current control valve features. Possible oscillations in flow control loop FIC. Threat of reactor temperature fluctuation due to variations in feed flow rate and composition.
lessons_learned: Improved pump reliability and stable operation
hazop_reason: Like-for-like replacement, no change to process design limits
change_description: It is proposed that to solve the excessive vibration and deteriorating performance of the feed preparation area P-101 feed pump, the replacement should be done. Although the new pump is likely to enhance reliability and energy efficiency, it will not change the characteristics of feed flow including pressure, flow rate, and stability.
system_impacts: P-101 directly feeds reactor R-201. Any variation in flow stability can affect reactor inlet conditions including flow and temperature coupling, catalyst reaction efficiency, and downstream fractionator load and separation performance.

name: MoC-003
description: Adjust reactor temperature setpoint to optimise catalyst performance and improve gasoline yield
title: Reactor R-201 Temperature Setpoint Adjustment
hazop_justification: HAZOP mandatory: alteration of critical process parameter. PSSR required: prior to working within new conditions.
engineering_risks: Heat build-up and deactivation of catalysts in reactors. Bigger coke growth that influences the performance of the regenerators. Existence of thermal imbalance between reactor and regenerator. New operating range instability of control loop.
lessons_learned: Improved yield with stable thermal control
change_description: The change in reactor temperature R-201 setpoint is a system-level change in the FCC Unit, and its effects spread over several interrelated regions. Reactor temperature change has a direct impact on reaction kinetics in the Reactor-Riser and consequently the catalyst activity, regenerator heat equilibrium and the subsequent separation of product downstream in the Fractionation section. This interdependency brings about the element of complexity since changes in temperature can affect the feed conversion efficiency, distribution of product yield and stability in operation. Besides, the change also affects control loops that control temperature, flow, and pressure, which enhances the chances of coupled system responses.
system_impacts: Directly impacts catalyst activity and coke formation. Influences regenerator load via coke burn-off. Affects downstream product distribution in fractionator. Interacts with air blower and combustion control system.
reason: Need to improve catalyst activity and process efficiency

name: MoC-002
description: Replace FV-103 with smart control valve to improve temperature regulation and enable remote monitoring

engineering_risks: Incorrect tuning of PID leading to temperature control oscillation. Sensor-actuator mismatch leading to delayed control system response. Integration errors in control systems commissioning. Threat of overheating or under heating of the reactor feed.
lessons_learned: Enhanced temperature control after tuning stabilization
change_description: The modification of the FV-103 control valve to a smart control valve will enhance the temperature regulation process in the feed heater. The change will also bring about advanced control such as remote control and improved feedback accuracy.
parameter_name: Temperature control accuracy and response time
system_impacts: The feed heater directly influences reactor inlet temperature. It influences the reaction kinetics of catalyst in R-201, influences the yield of products and selectivity, and influences the downstream separation in the fractionator.
reason: Inconsistent control performance and need for improved temperature stability

name: MoC-006
description: Install steam control valve and optimise steam injection to improve stripping efficiency
title: Catalyst Stripper Steam Optimization
hazop_justification: HAZOP required: direct impact on stripping efficiency and regenerator combustion behavior, interaction with thermodynamic balance and process emissions, involvement of control system modification affecting process stability. PSSR required: verification of valve installation, integrity, and control loop performance prior to startup.
engineering_risks: Excessive steam injection causing temperature imbalance. Insufficient stripping leading to hydrocarbon carryover and potential afterburn in the regenerator. Control loop instability due to improper tuning of steam flow regulation. Leakage risk at valve connections or flanges during commissioning. Potential disturbance propagation across interconnected process sections.
lessons_learned: Steam leakage incident required improved flange installation and inspection procedures
change_description: This scenario proposes enhancing stripping efficiency in the catalyst stripper S-301 by installing a steam flow control valve and optimizing the steam injection rate.
system_impacts: Stripping efficiency directly affects hydrocarbon carryover to the regenerator. Increased carryover impacts regenerator combustion load and emissions. Influences overall heat balance across the Reactor-Riser and Catalyst Regeneration sections. Affects downstream flue gas treatment and environmental compliance. Interacts with temperature and flow control loops within the FCC Unit.
reason: Improve stripping efficiency and reduce hydrocarbon carryover
